title: Metro Brands Ltd - 543426 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Metro Brands Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 14% and PAT about 13%, with April-May soft and June recovering to mid-teens-plus growth.
summary.overview: Standalone sales grew 14% and EBITDA 9% in Q1 FY27, with PAT up 13%, per management's opening remarks. April and May were soft on the U.S.-Iran conflict overhang and a shift in wedding dates, while June rebounded to a mid-teen double-digit gain. The e-commerce SOR (3P) channel slowed to 9%, while D2C and marketplace omni each grew about 60%. Management reiterated gross margin near 55-57% (quarter at almost 60%), EBITDA around 30%, and full-year PAT of 13-15%, citing marketing, treasury income, new-store dilution and talent/tech investment as PAT margin drivers.

financial_highlights.change: down roughly 200 bps YoY per analyst question; management cited about 200 bps delta
highest in past 5 quarters per management

segments.name: Clarks
segments.commentary: Women's range launched late CY2025 in about 200 MBOs, expanded to about 350 doors this spring, targeting 700 by year-end; men's range in under 100 stores. First Clarks EBOs from Q3 FY27, with a 100-150 store runway cited.

segments.name: FILA
segments.commentary: Opened 3 new EBOs and closed 1 legacy store (of 2 inherited); management said the brand is behind schedule, with acceleration expected toward end of FY27.

segments.name: MetroActiv / Walkway
segments.commentary: MetroActiv: 3 stores opened, 2 doing well and 1 underperforming, with BIS issues cited. Walkway: base of about 70 stores, over 30 opened in the quarter (about 50% growth), with mixed store performance.

segments.name: Crocs
segments.commentary: Growth was weaker pre-monsoon because June 2025 had strong monsoon demand that did not repeat in June 2026; management said Crocs is performing to plan now.

guidance_outlook: Full-year sales growth guided at about 15%, give or take a couple of points.
Full-year PAT guided at 13-15%; management said it expects to be around that range by year-end.
Gross margin guided at about 55-57%, EBITDA around 30%; Q1 gross margin is above that range.
E-commerce expected to grow 20-30% a year going forward; D2C and omni expected to stay double-digit for the year.
Some Diwali-linked sales expected to shift from Q2 into Q3 FY27 because Diwali falls later this year.
Store openings expected to return to a triple-digit annual pace, though Q1 net adds were only 9 (13 opened, 4 closed).
capex_capacity: New distribution centre of about 250,000 sq ft launched in March 2026 and is now fully operational with integrations complete.
Q1 FY27 opened 13 stores and closed 4 (net 9); FY26 had 140 openings and 20 closures.
Clarks EBO runway estimated at 100-150 stores; long-term sports runway of 300-500 stores across FILA EBO, Foot Locker and MetroActiv over 5-7 years.
Walkway medium-to-long-term target of ROCE of 25-30%, versus treasury yields of about 7-8%.
Management is testing a 2,000 sq ft store format and is still learning which markets can sustain it.
demand_pricing: April and May were soft from the U.S.-Iran conflict and a shift in Adhik Maas wedding dates (zero weddings in April and May per management); June rebounded to mid-teen double-digit growth.
Demand described as broad-based across price points, geographies and banners; management said it is not seeing it driven only by metros or Tier-3 cities.
Gross margin held near 60% through inventory discipline and forward buying 4-5 months ahead; normal inflationary price increases of 3-5%, with no direct oil-price impact yet.
Realisations up 6% YoY, mainly from mix (newer premium formats and Crocs), with full-year ASP growth expected at about 3-4%.
Premium 3,000+ price band at about 57% of sales (management said it is approaching 60%), with premiumisation expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why were April and May muted when peers held up, and was June materially stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited zero wedding dates in April and May and a consumer-sentiment distraction from the prolonged war. June rebounded strongly, helped by Crocs-friendly monsoon absence offset by other brands; the Crocs shortfall was timing-related.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SOR (3P) e-commerce slow, and will discounting cut growth?
qa_highlights.answer: SOR growth was lumpy from return-swap timing, plus a deliberate reduction in low price points and 3P discounts. Management expects e-com to grow well into double digits, with 20-30% a year as the healthy range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year margin outlook given wage hikes and input cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided gross margin 55-57% (currently above), EBITDA around 30%, and PAT 13-15%. Front-end wages are above state minimums, but wage rules will be absorbed as they change.

qa_highlights.question: Why not guide to 20% growth when demand is improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers measured guidance to avoid inventory overhang and brand-share loss; it guides to about 15% and says it aims higher. It cited three quarters of steady double-digit growth and rising conversion and new-customer counts.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the PAT margin decline and when does PAT growth return to mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps from top-of-funnel marketing, plus lower treasury income versus last year's teens yields, new-store dilution (about 40 Walkway stores among 140 openings), and talent/tech investment. Management expects a return to 15%-plus PAT growth as these normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Is BIS relief helping FILA launch timelines, and how is FILA inventory being discounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recent QC order allowing imports has no significant impact; ASEAN BIS renewals are the larger constraint. Heavy FILA discounting reflects legacy acquired inventory and 3-4 month sports life cycles with 9-month buying lead times.

risks_watch: BIS certification erraticism for factories, especially ASEAN suppliers and high-end athletic footwear, could constrain FILA and sports launches.
Input-cost inflation (RM, crude-linked) not yet in P&L per analyst; management says purchases are 4-5 months forward, so pressure may arrive in later quarters.
Minimum wage increases in certain states could raise front-end staff costs.
Treasury income normalisation and continued marketing investment may keep PAT margin below prior-year levels in the near term.
Diwali shift into Q3 could weigh on Q2 growth; FILA turnaround timing (late FY27) and MetroActiv and Walkway store productivity are open questions.
key_quotes: So, we guide to 15% for the year, give or take, a couple of points left or right of that.
But if you go after 20% and you only come in with 15%, that's absolutely fatal to a business.
It's still work in progress. It's not an easy thing to revive a brand that has been on discount for almost 18 months to 24 months.
But there is -- we're not out of the woods yet, specifically for high-end product in athletic.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery, brand health and the long-term store and e-commerce runway, but cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly declined to give forward-looking figures for July or FY27 beyond a ~15% sales and 13-15% PAT guide. Candid about soft April-May, FILA being behind schedule, and BIS-related supplier erraticism, which it said is "not out of the woods yet".

growth.why: Management guides full-year sales growth to about 15% (plus or minus a couple of points) and expects triple-digit store openings, but Q1 growth was 14% with April-May soft, net store adds only 9, and FILA behind schedule, so growth is positive but not backed by hard capacity figures.
